This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any memory leaks task, implementation, or piece of work complete.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Measure before optimizing any memory leaks bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
2. Validate memory leaks outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
3. When memory leaks decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
4. Keep memory leaks outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
5. Check that memory leaks terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
6. Before starting memory leaks work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
7. Re-check edge cases relevant to memory leaks (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid introducing new memory leaks abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Avoid mixing unrelated memory leaks concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of memory leaks correctness.
- Do not skip documenting memory leaks assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these memory leaks guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
